issues.description: LSP violation: _receive_messages no longer honors the supertype contract of bubbling/handling websocket disconnect
issues.detail: The base WebsocketService loop calling _receive_messages presumes the method either runs to natural completion when the socket closes or raises so the outer reconnect logic can act. The old code wrapped _process_messages in try/except and logged 'WebSocket connection closed' before returning. The new code removes that wrapper but the inner try/except inside the async-for still swallows generic Exception per-message. The postcondition 'on disconnect, return cleanly so the outer loop can reconnect' is now implicit and undocumented; if the async iterator raises (e.g., ConnectionClosed) it will now propagate up instead of being logged as before. That is a behavior change in the contract of this method that callers in websocket_service.py depend on. Either restore the outer try/except with the diagnostic log, or document explicitly that _receive_messages now propagates connection-closed exceptions and confirm the supertype loop handles them.

issues.description: SPEC-MISSING: the set of error message_types is a contract with ElevenLabs but is hardcoded as a tuple literal with no named constant or spec
issues.detail: The expanded error-type list is the abstract data type's discriminator for the 'error' variant of an inbound message. It should be a named module-level constant (e.g., ELEVENLABS_ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES) with a docstring linking to the ElevenLabs spec URL, so the contract is visible at the module boundary rather than buried in a conditional. As written, callers and future maintainers cannot tell what the abstraction promises about error handling without reading the branch.

issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry in the error message_type tuple
issues.detail: 'transcriber_error' appears twice in the membership tuple. Harmless at runtime (set membership semantics), but it signals the list was assembled without a spec check, and it weakens confidence that the full error taxonomy from the linked docs was transcribed correctly. A named frozenset constant would have made this impossible to overlook.

issues.description: LEAKY-ABSTRACTION: error_msg formatting collapses distinct error categories into one push_error shape
issues.detail: Previously auth_error and quota_exceeded_error had distinct prefixes ('Auth error:', 'Quota exceeded:') in the pushed error, giving downstream consumers a typed-ish discriminator. The unified branch now emits 'Error: {error_msg}' for all 14 categories, losing the category at the push_error boundary. If any caller branches on that prefix, this silently breaks them. Either include the message_type in the pushed payload (structured), or keep the category in the human-readable prefix. The abstraction's postcondition about what a downstream caller learns from a pushed error has been weakened without a spec update.

issues.description: Lost diagnostic: error-level logger.error for known error subtypes was removed
issues.detail: The old code emitted logger.error with category-specific context for error/auth_error/quota_exceeded_error before pushing the error frame. The new unified branch only calls push_error and drops the logger.error call entirely. Operators relying on logs (not just error frames) to diagnose ElevenLabs auth/quota failures will see a silent regression. Restore a logger.error with message_type included, or document that error frames are now the sole diagnostic surface.
changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline. Minor hygiene issue; many tools and linters expect POSIX text files to end with newline.

review.summary: The fix correctly identifies a real defect: the inner try/except in the old _receive_messages was swallowing connection-closed exceptions and preventing the outer websocket_service reconnect loop from doing its job. Removing it is the right structural move. However, the change leaves the supertype contract between _receive_messages and the websocket_service reconnect loop implicit — no comment, no docstring update, no acknowledgment that this method now propagates disconnect exceptions where it previously absorbed them. The error-handling consolidation flattens 14 message types into one tuple literal (with one duplicate, 'transcriber_error') and weakens the postcondition of push_error by collapsing category-specific prefixes and dropping the logger.error diagnostics. The abstract data type — 'inbound ElevenLabs message router' — would be cleaner with a named error-types constant and a documented contract for which exceptions propagate and which are logged-and-continued.
